newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 rises, shrugs of deputy PM resignation.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 rises, shrugs of deputy PM resignation.

text.p: Czech shares ignored the resignation of deputy Prime Minister Jan Kalvoda and rose strongly on Wednesday with heavy buying in the major issues pushing the PX50 and RPIX indices higher.
The PX50 gained 0.9 percent to 522.1 while the RPIX index of continuosly traded shares rose 1.1 percent to 1,083.7.
"The resignation may have some affect on forex but not on equities," said Miroslav Nosal of Patria Finance. "If there had been any impact it would have been in the blue chips," he added.
On Tuesday evening the deputy prime minister, who is also the justice minister, resigned after admitting he had falsely used the title of Doctor of Law.
Kalvoda is the head of the Civic Democratic Party (ODA) which is a junior partner in the coalition minority government.

Far from being held back by the Kalvoda affair, major issues had one of their best days in recent weeks. Leading the pack was SPT Telecom which ended 72 crowns higher on the bourse to 3,200, although dealers were at a loss to explain why.

"Interest in SPT came from abroad but I don't know why," said Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka. Kusacek said that the company was trading even higher late in the day on the over-the-counter market at around 3,235/3,265.
Among the other highly capitalised shares there were also some strong gains. Komercni Banka rose 39 crowns to 2,130 and CEZ was up eight crowns to 985.
Overall, turnover was heavier at 1.5 billion crowns.
